state_variables.u: deviation of short-range anthocyanin competence (Venosa-class MYB activity) from a homogeneous baseline

boundary_conditions: Periodic representative patch of petal epidermis. Diffusion is integrated in Fourier space. The displayed ocellus is the radially symmetric critical mode cos(k_c r) on a 200 by 150 grid upscaled to 800 by 600.

parameters.note: D_u and D_v are integers chosen so argmax sigma(k) lies on the assigned 259.2 µm scale. They are not the slot-176 placeholders alpha=1.55, beta=0.28, a=6, b=5, c=30.

equations: du/dt = f_u u + f_v v - c u^3 + D_u laplacian u
dv/dt = g_u u + g_v v + D_v laplacian v
Delta(k) = det(J) - h k^2 + D_u D_v k^4
empirical_claims: Shang et al. 2010: Venosa, an R2R3 MYB, places anthocyanin in epidermal cells overlying veins. That is a vein prepattern, not a published Turing wavelength of 259 µm.
Noda et al. 1994: MIXTA makes conical petal epidermal cells that intensify colour. Cell width is sub-wavelength relative to 259 µm (upper bound used here: 40 µm).
The gallery field's own 100 µm bar (111 px) gives a radial ring pitch of 77.8 µm. That measurement is independent of lambda_c and is not fitted to it.
A 10 mm petal lobe holds about 38.6 critical wavelengths. The whole flower is the scale successor of this slot.
